message.content:
Below is a quick‑look table of the **federal long weekends** that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the “observed” date is the nearest weekday; the long weekend is defined as the holiday plus the adjacent weekend days.)

| # | Holiday | Calendar Date | Observed (if different) | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---|---------|---------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | Monday Jan 2 | **Jan 1 – 3** |
| 2 | Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, etc.) | Monday Feb 20 | – | **Feb 18 – 20** |
| 3 | Good Friday | Friday Apr 7 | – | **Apr 7 – 9** |
| 4 | Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | – | **May 20 – 22** |
| 5 | Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 | – | **Jul 1 – 3** |
| 6 | Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | – | **Sep 2 – 4** |
| 7 | Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | – | **Oct 7 – 9** |
| 8 | Remembrance Day | Saturday Nov 11 | Friday Nov 10 | **Nov 10 – 12** |
| 9 | Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | – | **Dec 23 – 25** |

> **Notes**  
> * **Boxing Day (Dec 26)** is a federal holiday but it falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does **not** create a long weekend.  
> * Some provinces observe additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, Civic Holiday in Ontario, etc.). Those are not listed here because they are not federal holidays.  
> * If you need province‑specific long weekends, let me know and I can add those as well.
